subject: FY2015 Property Tax Rate And Allocation
overview: The council set the FY2015 property tax rate and merged the Fair Housing and Human Rights Commissions. A proposal to reduce the tax levy by $1 million using free cash failed, and a resolution for grant funding for a new peace garden was tabled pending further maintenance details.

items.title: FY2015 Tax Levy Reduction Debate
items.summary: A motion to reduce the FY2015 property tax levy by approximately $1 million using certified free cash failed following an extensive debate regarding the necessity of maintaining municipal reserves and potential state aid cuts. Supporters argued for providing relief to taxpayers, while opponents cited fiscal stability concerns and upcoming capital needs like a new police station.

items.title: Tax Rate and Exemptions Approval
items.summary: The council approved the minimum residential factor of 0.899216 for fiscal year 2015, ensuring a shift of the tax burden to commercial and industrial properties. Proposals to adopt open space, residential, and small commercial tax exemptions were all rejected.

items.title: Legal Settlements
items.summary: Approved personal injury settlements for Adelina Palermo and Sharon Deioso related to accidents involving city property.

items.title: Human Rights Commission Merger
items.summary: Approved an ordinance merging the Fair Housing Commission and the Human Rights Commission into a single entity with expanded protections including gender identity and genetic information. The new nine-member commission is intended to streamline efforts to address civil rights and housing issues.

items.title: Coffee with a Cop Program
items.summary: Authorized the police department to implement the 'Coffee with a Cop' community outreach program to foster better communication between officers and residents.

items.title: Crystal Campbell Peace Garden
items.summary: Tabled a resolution to accept state grant funding and other donations for the $1.1 million Crystal Campbell Peace Garden. The council requested a detailed maintenance plan and cost breakdown before authorizing the project.

items.title: Free Cash and Water Rate Reports
items.summary: Approved a request for a detailed breakdown of free cash accounts from the last three years and discussed resident concerns regarding the newly implemented tiered water rate system.

items.title: Condolences and Adjournment
items.summary: Extended condolences to the family of teacher Bill Carter and observed a moment of silence for Mary Butler before adjourning.
